We run a small chain of shared offices and want RoomFlow to handle our meeting rooms properly. Right now people book
rooms in a spreadsheet and it is a mess.

Members should see every room in their building with its size, what is in it (screen, whiteboard, video call kit) and
which times are free today and this week. They pick a free time, say how long and how many people are coming, and book
it. A member can book at most 4 hours a day across all rooms, and never more than 2 weeks ahead. If they come with
guests, they type the guests' names so reception knows who to let in.

Members get an email right after booking, and a reminder 15 minutes before the meeting starts. They can move or cancel
their own booking up to an hour before. After that, cancelling still frees the room but counts as a late cancel; three
late cancels in a month and the member cannot book for the next 7 days.

Reception staff need a simple daily view: which rooms are booked, by whom, and which guests are expected, so they can
print guest badges in the morning. They can also book a room for a member who calls in, and they can mark a guest as
arrived.

Building managers set up the rooms: name, floor, size, opening hours, and whether a room needs approval. Some big rooms
need a manager to approve the booking first; the member sees the booking as waiting until then and gets an email when it
is approved or turned down, with the manager's reason.

Managers also want a monthly report per building: how many hours each room was used, how many bookings were cancelled
late, and which members booked the most. They download it as a spreadsheet for the finance team, because some members
pay extra for big rooms.

Members who pay extra rooms get an invoice at the end of the month listing each paid booking. Finance staff can mark an
invoice as paid and send a reminder for unpaid ones.

When a room is closed for cleaning or repairs, a manager blocks it for those days. Bookings already made in that time
are cancelled for the members, and they get an email offering the nearest free room of the same size.

On a phone, members mostly want to see today's bookings, check in when they arrive (so the room is not given away after
10 minutes) and find a free room right now. If nobody checks in within 10 minutes, the room becomes free again and the
booking counts as a no-show.

Everyone signs in with their work email. Staff and managers only see the buildings they work in.
